chapter: Touring abroad and the future of music
title: Japan, worldwide interest in jazz, and bootlegs
summary: He has toured most of the world; American jazz is widely wanted, and Poland learned it underground during the war.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What about on the other side of our continent, in Asia? Now, you've been to Japan. What, more than once that you've been there?
No, I've never been to Japan but once.
Yeah. That was in the '60s then. That was a long time.

Yeah, and it included places like Hong Kong and -- oh, what's the country where -- oh, great art and everything. Well, anyway, I've been to most parts of the world by now and I find a great deal of interest for American music, and above all American jazz music. And that has lasting power, and I
think it's important and we should utilize it every chance we have.

Now, you've -- both of us are aware and many people, a good deal of your many recordings are, like, black market, in a sense. People just grab onto them when they're available. That seems to be everywhere. It means several things. Somebody is trying to make some money, but at the same time there's a demand for this music.

Yeah, there's a desire to hear the music. It started with the -- it's the way that Poland became aware of American jazz music or any kind of music, during the wartime periods and all, when it was all underground. And yet, it was more prevalent than probably some of our biggest American cities.
And so this is a very healthy scene and I'm very proud of the fact that I have been able to go to some of these places.
